official.description: The SMU Merit Scholarship is a merit-based undergraduate award from Singapore Management University for Singapore Citizens entering a full-time degree programme, of which up to 35 are awarded each year. It provides a full four-year subsidised tuition fee waiver for regular terms from Academic Year 2027-28, a S$12,000 growth opportunities allowance for overseas community service and global exposure, and Student Success Centre development opportunities. The scholarship is bond-free and publishes no living allowance.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a top-tier, bond-free tuition waiver for Singapore Citizens, but the money is concentrated in fees and a single S$12,000 overseas-exposure pot - there is no living stipend, so you still need to fund daily life yourself. Because there is no separate scholarship form, your one shot is to tick the scholarship box inside the admission application and write a strong scholarship essay early, since the referee letter and the panel interview both happen inside the same admissions cycle. Treat the published AY2027-28 benefit wording as the figures that will govern the next intake and watch SMU's Important Dates page for the window to open.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singapore Citizen school leavers with strong A-Level or polytechnic results plus a sustained leadership and CCA/community record who want four years of fees covered without a bond.
application_readiness_checklist: Draft the scholarship personal essay before the application window opens - it mirrors the admissions essay workload and is easiest to do while results are fresh
Nominate a tutor or principal as referee well before you submit; the recommendation is submitted online by the referee, so a late nomination risks an incomplete application
Prepare evidence of leadership and co-curricular/community impact that can be compressed into the essay, since shortlisting runs on non-academic record strength
Rehearse for a panel interview focused on leadership trajectory and community impact, not just grades
From November, check SMU's Important Dates page daily for the next intake's opening and closing dates and apply in the first weeks, not the last
common_rejection_risks: Weak personal essay or thin co-curricular/community record - shortlisting is explicitly on non-academic strength as well as academics
Referee recommendation never submitted online because the nomination came too late
Assuming the scholarship fills living costs and under-budgeting, then struggling financially in Year 1
Missing the admissions application window entirely - there is no later scholarship-only route for prospective students until the January current-student round on OASIS
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living expenses in Singapore, any special-term (semester 3) tuition since the waiver covers regular terms only, annual/miscellaneous fees, and any overseas programme costs above the S$12,000 growth opportunities allowance - all self-funded.
document_audit: The essay lives inside the admission application portal, so a browser or account problem late on deadline night costs you both admission and scholarship consideration
Referee letters are uploaded by the referee, not you - there is no document you can chase at the last minute if the referee misses the window
Optional does not mean unimportant: SMU states applicants are strongly encouraged to obtain the tutor/principal recommendation
alerts: The published tuition waiver and allowance apply 'starting from Academic Year 2027-28', so confirm the figures for your own cohort on the scholarship page before relying on them
Up to 35 awards a year against a full Singapore Citizen freshmen intake - this is genuinely competitive, not a blanket waiver
Interviews are in person at SMU for shortlisted applicants, with notifications released in batches between January and July - keep the whole period free rather than assuming an early date
Only regular terms (semesters 1 and 2) are waived; special-term tuition is not covered

SMU's Financial Aid FAQ states recipients must maintain the minimum CGPA stated in their scholarship agreement (the FAQ cites 3.4 out of 4.0) and may not hold another similar award without prior written approval
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One submission: complete the SMU online admission application, indicate scholarship interest in its Scholarship section, submit the essay online, and wait for a batched shortlist notification that leads to an in-person panel interview at SMU.

official.description: The Temasek Undergraduate Local Scholarship is a merit-based award from Temasek, administered by the Singapore Institute of Technology, offered to polytechnic graduates enrolling in full-time STEM undergraduate programmes at SIT. Each scholarship is valued at up to S$18,030 per annum including an annual stipend of S$7,200, with a one-time S$2,000 laptop allowance and a possible one-time S$10,000 Global Mobility Grant. It forms part of Temasek's S$150 million T-Spring community gift marking the company's 50th anniversary in 2024, with mentorship and networking support for scholars' professional aspirations.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an annual, bond-free award administered by SIT rather than a single four-year package: the value is capped at S$18,030 per year and the Global Mobility Grant only appears if you are eligible for and accept a University-run global exposure programme. You apply as a matriculated SIT student through IN4SIT when the round opens in July, not through the SIT admissions application, so the practical sequence is to secure your SIT place first and watch your SIT e-mail for the scholarship window. Budget for living costs above the S$7,200 stipend and for any remaining fee balance yourself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Polytechnic graduates who have gained a place on a full-time STEM degree at SIT, are Singapore citizens, and want a fee-and-stipend top-up that leaves no bond attached.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure admission and matriculate at SIT first - the online scholarship form sits in IN4SIT, which matriculated students access
In June, ask a referee for an endorsed Letter of Recommendation so it is ready when the July round opens
Keep your SIT Record of Achievement accessible for upload where applicable
Set up and keep active a Credit Bank Account in IN4SIT so payment can be credited net of outstanding fees
Watch your SIT e-mail in July for the round announcement and the exact deadline, since no calendar date is published
common_rejection_risks: Waiting for a published closing date that never appears and missing the deadline communicated only by SIT e-mail
Applying before matriculating, when the IN4SIT form is not yet accessible
Holding another scholarship or sponsorship that overlaps beyond tuition fees in the same academic year without prior University approval
Losing the active IN4SIT Credit Bank Account, which blocks disbursement net of outstanding fees
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything above the S$18,030 annual cap: higher-fee programme balance, accommodation, daily living costs beyond the S$7,200 stipend, and global exposure programme costs beyond the S$10,000 grant. Since the donated-award terms describe a one-year award with an annual re-application round, treat each year's funding as needing renewal rather than guaranteed.
document_audit: The recommendation must be endorsed by the referee - an unendorsed or self-submitted letter will not meet the published requirement
The SIT Record of Achievement is required only 'where applicable', so check which cohort it applies to before assuming you can skip it
Because the award is credited net of outstanding fees in IN4SIT, unpaid fee balances silently reduce the cash you actually receive
alerts: SIT's donated-award Terms and Conditions describe the award as a one-time award tenable for one academic year, even though the value is published per annum - plan around annual re-application, not automatic renewal
No deadline is published anywhere on the official pages; the only reliable signal is the July round announcement sent to your SIT e-mail
Donor stewardship is expected: thank-you letters to Temasek and attendance at donor events can form part of holding the award
The S$10,000 Global Mobility Grant is conditional - it is not part of the headline S$18,030 and requires eligibility for plus enrolment in a University-conducted programme
SIT's terms may be updated at any time on its website and take effect from posting, so re-read the Terms and Conditions each year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Gain an SIT place and matriculate, then apply through the IN4SIT online scholarship form when the July round opens, uploading the endorsed recommendation and Record of Achievement before the emailed deadline.
